reason: Both answers correctly diagnose the problem (MTTR is a mean, and incident splitting, clock changes and recurrence can all lower it) and recommend SLO and error-budget burn as the primary metric. B adds a verified worked example (10×60 min vs 30×36 min gives MTTR down 40% and total downtime up 80%). It also covers severity downgrading and reclassification, and it checks for definition, alert and tooling changes, which addresses the Goodhart angle more directly. It separates time to detect from time to mitigate and adds change failure rate. A's unique points are unlogged toil and a next-step line, which B's "check first" list already covers. Neither contains an error. B is somewhat more actionable and covers more of the key points.
